question.text: The intensity of γ - radiation from a given source is I. On passing through 36 mm of lead, it is reduced to I8. Assuming that the intensity in transmitted radiation varies exponentially with the thickness of the material, then the thickness of lead, which will reduce the intensity to I2, will be

solution.text:
On passing through lead, the intensity of γ - radiation decreases exponentially with the thickness traversed and is given by

I=I0e-μx , where μ is the absorption coefficient of the lead.

In the first case, when x=36 mm, I=I08

 I08=I0 e-μ×36

⇒loge8=36μ

In the second case,

I=I02

Let x be the thickness of the lead sheet, then

I02=I0 e-μx

loge⁡2=μx

μx36μ=loge2loge8

x=36×loge⁡2loge⁡23=36×loge⁡23loge⁡2

x=12 mm

question.text: Cathode rays of velocity 106 m s-1 describe an approximately circular path of radius 1 m in an electric field 300 V m-1. If the velocity of cathode rays are doubled. The value of electric field so that the rays describe the same circular path, will be

solution.text:
Cathode rays are composed of electrons, when they move in electric field a force

                                             F=eE    ...(i)

Acts on them, this provides the necessary centripetal force to the particles

F=mv2r   ...(ii)

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

eE=mv2r

⇒                            r=mv2eE=m1062e(300)     ...(iii)

When velocity is doubled same circular path is followed, hence radius is same

r=m2×1062eE   ...(iv)

Equating Eqs. (iii) and (iv), we get

m×1062300e=m×2×1062eE

⇒                 E=300×4=1200 V cm-1
